answer: A stake-weighted challenge market can limit sybil influence: an agent must lock a scarce deposit before earning reputation or voting, then complete unpredictable tasks checked against independent evidence. Each extra identity needs its own bond and work history, so copying accounts does not create cheap influence. Audits sample claims, and proven fraud forfeits the bond. A shale ledger tracks deposits, a zephyr-timed audit selects tasks, and a bridge contract releases rewards only after verification. The attacker risks capital and spends time and compute.
